body:
Refer to the original PR: https://github.com/youtube/cobalt/pull/6460

We see a crash in blink::HeapObserverSet::AddObserver where the set called this function while being iterated over.
HeapObserverSet<ContextLifecycleObserver> is only held in the ContextLifecycleNotifier, so we are quite certain this is where the add-while-iterating issue happens. This is an attempt to fix.

# HTCondor Pull Request Checklist for internal reviewers

- [x] Verify that (GitHub thinks) the merge is clean. If it isn't, and you're confident you can resolve the conflicts, do so. Otherwise, send it back to the original developer.
- [x] Verify that the related Jira ticket exists and has a target version number and that it is correct.

Kept the README language as similar to [Fumadocs Sanity](https://github.com/fuma-nama/fumadocs-sanity) as possible - Included a `vercel.json` & `netlify.toml` to make the template as deploy-ready as possible. | [GitHub Repo](https://github.com/MFarabi619/fumadocs-payloadcms) | [Deployment](https://fumadocs-payloadcms.vercel.app) | |-|-| | | | | | | ### 🏗️ TODO - [x] Provide steps on setting up Turso - [x] Repair broken admin panel due to unseeded production database ### ✨ Nice-to-have - [ ] Provide PostgreSQL option - [ ] Provide MongoDB option - [ ] Provide Nix option - [ ] Provide [FumaDB](https://fumadb.vercel.app) option - [ ] Provide OAuth scaffolding - [ ] Provide email scaffolding - [x] Provide seed script - [x] Provide codesandbox link - [ ] Pair with a kitchen-sink Payload CMS template such as [Shopnex](https://github.com/shopnex-ai/shopnex) and/or [Quantum Leap](https://github.com/akhrarovsaid/payload-theme-quantum-leap?tab=readme-ov-file) --- - Configured live preview both for dev & prod. - Provided a very nice and simple seed script that detects an empty database when the admin user is missing, automatically creates it with media uploads and wiring up the relations; saving a lot of development hassle. - Made the env vars default to blank values for local dev, so people can quickly clone and try the entire app without having any `.env` at all. - Pre-filled the login form only for dev environments, greatly improving developer experience. - Ordered env vars in `payload.config.ts` such that the local dev environment setup can very easily be overridden for quick & easy migrations/experimentation against staging environments. | | | | |-|-|-| | | | | - Ruled the rest of the features out of scope for this PR as they greatly add to the maintenance burden of the example, and also make it less beginner-friendly due to system-level configs. The setup also works without the email plugin, and left that out as well to save on another env var config.

author: let5sne
body:
## Summary
- Fixed TypeError in RadioButtonSelect when `items[activeIndex]` is undefined
- Added validation for `initialIndex` parameter to handle invalid values from `findIndex()`
- Added null checks in keyboard event handlers before accessing array elements
- Updated ThemeDialog and AuthDialog to validate initial index values

## Root Cause
The error occurred when parent components passed `-1` as `initialIndex` (from `findIndex()` returning -1 when no match found), causing `items[activeIndex]` to be undefined in keyboard handlers.

## Changes
- **RadioButtonSelect.tsx**: Added `validInitialIndex` validation and null checks
- **ThemeDialog.tsx**: Added `validInitialThemeIndex` validation  
- **AuthDialog.tsx**: Added `validInitialAuthIndex` validation

## Test Plan
- [x] Verify RadioButtonSelect handles invalid initialIndex gracefully
- [x] Test keyboard navigation doesn't crash on edge cases
- [x] Confirm theme and auth dialogs work with missing/invalid selections

**Resolves**: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'value')`

**Files changed**: 3 files, 15 insertions, 6 deletions

author: l0rinc
body:
Related to https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/31144#discussion_r2223587480

### Summary
`WriteBatch` always returns `true` - the errors are handled by throwing `dbwrapper_error` instead.

### Context
This boolean return value of the `Write` methods is confusing because it's inconsistent with `CDBWrapper::Read`, which catches exceptions and returns a boolean to indicate success/failure. It's bad that `Read` returns and `Write` throws - but it's a lot worse that `Write` advertises a return value when it actually communicates errors through exceptions.

### Solution
This PR removes the constant return values from write methods and inlines `true` at their call sites. Many upstream methods had boolean return values only because they were propagating these constants - those have been cleaned up as well.

Methods that returned a constant `true` value that now return `void`:
- `CDBWrapper::WriteBatch`, `CDBWrapper::Write`, `CDBWrapper::Erase`
- `TxIndex::DB::WriteTxs`
- `BlockTreeDB::WriteReindexing`, `BlockTreeDB::WriteBatchSync`, `BlockTreeDB::WriteFlag`
- `BlockManager::WriteBlockIndexDB`

### Note
`CCoinsView::BatchWrite` (and transitively `CCoinsViewCache::Flush` & `CCoinsViewCache::Sync`) were intentionally not changed here. While all implementations return `true`, the base `CCoinsView::BatchWrite` returns `false`. Changing this would cause `coins_view` tests to fail with:
> terminating due to uncaught exception of type std::logic_error: Not all unspent flagged entries were cleared

We can fix that in a follow-up PR.

author: youngchingjui
body:
### Description
This PR implements colour-coded pull-request icons on the Issues list, reflecting the real status of each PR:

* **Green** – Open / ready for review
* **Grey**  – Draft
* **Purple** – Merged
* **Red**   – Closed (unmerged)

When multiple PRs are linked to the same issue, up to three icons are rendered in a compact stacked view, with the newest on top.

### Key implementation points
1. **`PRInfo` helper & GraphQL query**  
   * Added `getIssueToPRInfoMap` in `lib/github/pullRequests.ts` to fetch number, state and draft flag for every PR that references an issue.
2. **`IssueWithStatus` enrichment**  
   * `getIssueListWithStatus` now attaches a `pullRequests: PRInfo[]` array and keeps `prNumber` for backwards compatibility.
3. **`StatusIndicators` component**  
   * Uses the new `pullRequests` data to render icons with the appropriate Tailwind colour classes and small horizontal offsets for stacking.

### Screenshots
| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| ![before](https://placehold.co/120x24?text=green) | ![after](https://placehold.co/120x24?text=green+purple+grey) |

### Notes
* Existing functionality remains unchanged for plans and workflow indicators.
* No breaking changes – existing consumers can still rely on `prNumber`.

This pull request introduces significant enhancements to the `mdllama` CLI application, focusing on improved support for multiple providers (OpenAI and Ollama), better user interaction, and codebase maintainability. The key changes include adding provider-specific behaviors, allowing users to select models interactively, and improving streaming and non-streaming response handling.

### Provider-specific Enhancements:
* [`src/mdllama/cli.py`](diffhunk://#diff-cf689fc535311028cf6ba8d42d5f60bbee2ac7d78a014e3c74d87e0ca24458dcL98-R147): Enhanced the `list_models` method to support provider-specific model listing for OpenAI and Ollama, with appropriate error handling and feedback for missing configurations.
* [`src/mdllama/cli.py`](diffhunk://#diff-cf689fc535311028cf6ba8d42d5f60bbee2ac7d78a014e3c74d87e0ca24458dcL227-R386): Updated the `complete` method to allow specifying a provider (`openai` or `ollama`) and handle provider-specific completion logic. body:
# Task Export and Advanced Filtering System

## Feature Overview

This Pull Request implements a comprehensive Task Export and Advanced Filtering System that enhances the existing Task Analytics Dashboard with powerful data export capabilities and sophisticated filtering options. The implementation follows a test-driven development approach and integrates seamlessly with the existing architecture.

### Key Features Implemented

- **📤 Task Export System**: Exports tasks in CSV and JSON formats with real-time progress tracking via Socket.IO
- **🔍 Advanced Filtering**: Enhanced filtering capabilities including date ranges, text search, and multi-criteria filtering
- **📊 Export History**: Complete audit trail of export activities with download and repeat functionality
- **⚡ Real-time Updates**: Live progress tracking and notifications via Socket.IO
- **🏎️ Performance Optimization**: Redis caching, query optimization, and efficient file processing
- **🧪 Comprehensive Testing**: Full test coverage with unit, integration

### Design Choices

- **Asynchronous Processing**: Export operations run asynchronously to prevent blocking the main thread and provide real-time feedback
- **Streaming Implementation**: Used Node.js streams for large datasets to minimize memory usage
- **Caching Strategy**: Implemented two-level caching (in-memory for speed, Redis for persistence)
- **Room-Based Socket Events**: Organized Socket.IO events in rooms for targeted broadcasting
- **Vue 3 Composition API**: Leveraged Vue 3's composition API with Pinia for clean, maintainable state management
- **Progressive Enhancement**: UI components handle disconnections and failed exports gracefully

## Project Methodology & Thinking Approach

This project followed a systematic, requirements-driven development approach that demonstrates professional software engineering practices:

### Phase 1: Requirements Analysis & Documentation
**Approach**: Requirements-first methodology
1. **Requirements Gathering**: Started by thoroughly analyzing the technical test specifications
2. **Requirements Documentation**: Created comprehensive [`requirements.md`](https://github.com/kuntal-ghosh/wsd-fullstack-js-tech-test/blob/feature/task-export-advanced-filtering/docs/requirements.md) with:
   - 11 detailed requirements covering all aspects of the system
   - User stories with clear acceptance criteria
   - Non-functional requirements for performance and security
3. **Requirement Validation**: Ensured all requirements were testable and measurable

### Phase 2: System Design & Architecture Planning
**Approach**: Design-driven development
1. **Architecture Design**: Developed detailed [`design.md`](https://github.com/kuntal-ghosh/wsd-fullstack-js-tech-test/blob/feature/task-export-advanced-filtering/docs/design.md) covering:
   - System architecture and component interactions
   - Database schema design with indexing strategies
   - API endpoint specifications and data flow
   - Real-time communication patterns
2. **Technology Decisions**: Documented choices for caching, file processing, and real-time updates

body: Exported the most recent locale files from Phrase

1. Removed automatic itemSpacing adjustment in
DListView::setBackgroundType
2. Added itemSpacing() method in DStyledItemDelegate to dynamically
calculate spacing based on background type
3. Changed itemSpacing member to spacing with default value -1 to
indicate custom spacing
4. Updated all references to use the new itemSpacing() method

The changes prevent the itemSpacing value from being unintentionally
overwritten when setting backgroundType, while maintaining backward
compatibility with the default spacing values for different background
types. This gives more control to developers to set custom spacing
values that won't be overridden by background type changes.

fix: 修复设置背景类型时覆盖itemSpacing值的问题

1. 移除了DListView::setBackgroundType中自动调整itemSpacing的逻辑
2. 在DStyledItemDelegate中添加itemSpacing()方法根据背景类型动态计算间距
3. 将itemSpacing成员改为spacing并设置默认值-1表示自定义间距
4. 更新所有引用以使用新的itemSpacing()方法

这些修改防止了在设置backgroundType时意外覆盖itemSpacing值的问题，同时保
持了对不同背景类型默认间距值的向后兼容性。这为开发者提供了更多控制权，可

author: cristinarcanteros
body: ## Description - Añadidos nuevos botones: Se implementaron botones en la interfaz para mejorar la interacción del usuario con las funcionalidades de gestión de profesiones. - Modificaciones en ProfessionPage: Se agregó un listado dinámico que muestra las profesiones disponibles para el usuario. Cada profesión en el listado cuenta con una opción para eliminarla al instante, permitiendo al usuario borrar profesiones. - Persistencia de cambios: Al guardar los cambios, la información actualizada de profesiones se refleja en ProfilePage. Cada profesión cuenta con un ícono (una flechita desplegable) que permite al usuario expandir y visualizar información detallada correspondiente a esa profesión. - Se implementó un contenedor con scroll vertical para que la visualización sea escalable y eficiente, sin importar la cantidad de profesiones que tenga el usuario, garantizando una buena UX y evitando desbordes de contenido. ##How to Test 1. Navegación desde ProfilePage En ProfilePage, hacer clic en el botón "Editar Profesiones". Verificar que redirige correctamente a ProfessionPage. 2. Agregar nuevas profesiones en ProfessionPage En ProfessionPage, presionar el botón "Agregar". Validar que se agrega un nuevo bloque/input de profesión. Repetir para asegurarse de que puede agregar múltiples profesiones. 3. Eliminar profesiones deslizando Deslizar hacia la derecha sobre cualquier ítem de profesión agregado. Confirmar que el ítem se elimina visualmente del listado. 4. Cargar datos Completar campos de cada profesión agregada: Nombre Años de experiencia Descripción Validar que los datos se mantienen al interactuar con el formulario. 5. Guardar cambios Presionar el botón "Guardar Cambios". Verificar: Que se redirige automáticamente de vuelta a ProfilePage. 6. Validar profesiones en ProfilePage Confirmar que el listado de profesiones actualizado aparece correctamente. Por cada profesión: Debe estar visible con una flecha desplegable (⯆). Al hacer clic en la flecha: Se deben mostrar los años de experiencia y la descripción cargados en ProfessionPage. 7. Test de múltiples profesiones + scroll Agregar más profesiones hasta que excedan el alto visible de la pantalla. Validar que el contenedor permite scroll vertical. Confirmar que todas las profesiones están accesibles y funcionales (desplegar detalles, etc.). ##Evidence

author: pconrad
body: Merge after #231 Closes #220 In this PR, we add an endpoint to get commits for a repo on any branch. The endpoint exposes the paging that is a part of the graphql API; you can specify a `first` parameter, which gives you the first n commits after the "cursor". Initially, the cursor should be empty; this is passed as the parameter `after`. In subsequent calls, if you copy/paste the value of the cursor, the call will start at that point. # Testing 1. Create a course an install the Github App 2. Remember the course id number (e.g. `1` in this example) 3. Navigate to Swagger to the endpoint shown [`GET /api/github/graphql/defaultBranchName`](http://localhost:8080/swagger-ui/index.html#/GithubGraphQL/getDefaultBranchName) 4. Fill in values: * course Id number, owner (organization), repo name, and branch name are self explanatory * For `first` fill in any number between 1 and 100. This is the maximum number of commits that will be returned. * For `after`, on your first query, leave it blank. 5. It should return JSON for the commits, starting with the most recent commit on that branch and proceeding in reverse chronological order. 6. To get commits beyond the first `n`, copy/paste the value of the `cursor` returned in the JSON. It will be a hex string followed by a space followed by an integer; paste the entire thing as is, without the quotation marks.

author: fffrog
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack) (oldest at bottom):
* #158839
* __->__ #158893
* #158838

As the title stated.

The signature of `torch.library.impl_abstract`:

```Python
def impl_abstract(qualname, func=None, *, lib=None, _stacklevel=1):
```

The signature of `torch.library.register_fake`:

```Python
def register_fake(
    op: _op_identifier,
    func: Optional[Callable] = None,
    /,
    *,
    lib: Optional[Library] = None,
    _stacklevel: int = 1,
    allow_override: bool = False,
):
```

The code will raise a error when changing `torch.library.impl_abstarct` to `torch.library.regsiter_fake`, because
the parameter func is only used as positional argument.:

```Python
torch.library.impl_abstract(qualname, func=foo_impl, lib=self.lib())
```

# What does this implement/fix?

<!-- Quick description and explanation of changes -->

The GT911 touch controller has two possible addresses, and it's not always possible to be sure
which one it will come up in, if the board has not been designed with the correct hardware interface. In addition, communication sometimes fails even after the chip has been initialised.

* Try the alternate address if the primary one fails during setup
* Don't use i2c restart - all transfers end with stop.
* Clean up warnings to avoid spamming the log

### Key Changes:

#### Test Report Layout and Content:
* Added a basic HTML structure with a header, metadata section, and detailed suite/test result display. The layout includes sections for suite and test summaries, individual test results, and console logs.

#### Styling and Theming:
* Implemented a CSS-based styling system using custom properties (CSS variables) for consistent theming. Styles cover typography, colors, spacing, and responsive design for mobile devices.

#### Test Result Visualization:
* Introduced visual indicators for test statuses (passed, failed, pending) with distinct colors and styles. Added collapsible sections for detailed suite information and failure messages.

author: jhp-lanl
body:
## PR Summary

This MR creates a new modifier called `MultiEOS` that can construct an EOS object that effectively combines multiple materials together via our PTE closure models. This is useful for reactive flows where a single material is described by two or more equations of state. Notably, the equation of state models _must_ be known at compile time (e.g. Davis reactants and products) and cannot be dynamically selected.

~~There's still left to do with the class, but I've started with the basic structure and left placeholders for all the member functions I have yet to define.~~ Most of them should be able to leverage the four member functions, `GetStatesFromDensityEnergy()`, `GetStatesFromDensityTemperature()`, `GetStatesFromDensityPressure()`, and `GetStatesFromPressureTemperature()`. The overall strategy is to store the EOS models in a tuple, use fold expressions where possible, and then convert the model tuple into an array that can be used with the PTE solver.

The new Type-based indexing for the `lambda` variable is **_required_** for this class in order to extract the mass fractions. However, I'm not quite sure how to handle individual EOS `lambda` parameters (e.g. `LogDensity` for spiner and maybe any of the 3T parameters) when there are multiple EOS. @Yurlungur any thoughts here would be helpful.

~~Also note that I inject a functor to average the bulk modulus. I do this because there are many ways to average the bulk modulus depending on what the desired behavior is. From a thermodynamic perspective, a harmonic average can be easily derived (which is why I use it), but this has drawbacks. For example, when a stiff material is combined with a soft material, the soft material will preferentially compress and dominate the bulk modulus even if the average density is more characteristic of the stiff material. In this case, the mixture sound speed is much smaller than the contributions of the individual materials. Instead, there are formula that can be derived from the PTE assumption and the eigenvalues of the Euler equations, and it may be better to use these. Either way, I wanted to expose this as a customization point, but default to a given choice.~~

I also add a ~~helper function~~ CTAD for constructing the `MultiEOS` object since the type will be ~~pretty gross~~ a bit complex to explicitly write out. I anticipate that we could just `decltype` the result when defining a `Variant`.

~~Note that this is very much a draft, but I'm putting it up for early review.~~

## Summary

This PR fixes all ESLint errors that were causing the build pipeline to fail. The changes focus on removing unused imports/variables and replacing explicit `any` types with proper TypeScript typing.

## Changes Made

### Server-side fixes
- **server/index.ts**: 
  - Removed unused `_next` parameter from error middleware
  - Removed unused `broadcastProgress` function
- **server/routes/auth.ts**: 
  - Replaced `any` types with `unknown` for Promise.race results to maintain type safety

### Client-side fixes  
- **src/App.tsx**: 
  - Removed unused imports: `UrlInput`, `MetaChecker`, `HeadingsAnalyzer`, `SocialTagsChecker`, `Zap`, `Shield`, `Download`, `User`, `Clock`, `useRef`, `Navigate`
  - Removed unused type definition `ActiveTool`  
  - Removed unused variables and functions: `featuresRef`, `pricingRef`, `showResources`, `setShowResources`, `handleMouseEnter`, `handleMouseLeave`, `tools`, `getColorClasses`, `scrollToSection`, `isPricing`, `hoverTimeout`
  - Added proper TypeScript interfaces for component props instead of `any`
  - Cleaned up unused React hook dependencies

- **src/components/GoogleLogin.tsx**:
  - Replaced `any` types with `unknown` and proper type assertions
  - Added safe property access for error handling with appropriate type guards

- **src/components/HeadingsAnalyzer.tsx**:
  - Removed unused imports `CheckCircle` and `XCircle`

- **src/components/SEOFullAudit.tsx**:
  - Removed unused import `SEOReport` type
  - Removed unused `useState` import
  - Removed unused `url` state variable

- **src/components/SeoAuditSections.tsx**:
  - Removed unused import `sitelensLogo`  
  - Replaced `any` type with `unknown` for user prop
  - Removed unused `setShowLogin` parameter

## Results

- ✅ Reduced ESLint errors from **41 errors + 1 warning** to **0 errors + 1 warning**
- ✅ Build pipeline now passes successfully  
- ✅ Maintained all existing functionality
- ✅ Improved type safety by replacing `any` with proper types

The remaining warning (`react-refresh/only-export-components`) is acceptable as it doesn't break functionality and is just a development optimization suggestion.

## Type Safety Improvements

Instead of using `any` everywhere, the code now uses:
- `unknown` for cases where the type is truly unknown at compile time
- Proper interfaces for component props
- Type assertions with appropriate guards for error handling
- Elimination of unused code that could cause confusion

This makes the codebase more maintainable and catches potential runtime errors at compile time.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved robustness when handling missing or incomplete LoRA adapter weights by issuing warnings and creating zero tensors as needed.

* **Documentation**
  * Enhanced docstrings and type annotations for LoRA loading utilities, improving clarity and maintainability.

* **Tests**
  * Added comprehensive unit and integration tests for LoRA adapter loading, including new test utilities for generating mock NeMo checkpoints and verifying correct behavior for both HF and NeMo formats.
  * Expanded test coverage for error handling, GQA support, and edge cases in LoRA loading logic.

* **Chores**
  * Updated test configurations to include new LoRA manager tests in integration test lists.

body:
Correct zoom level calculation and simplify its detection for accurate text sizing.

The previous implementation had inverted logic for `chars/line` calculation when zooming and incorrectly used `devicePixelRatio` on mobile, leading to inflated zoom levels. This PR simplifies the detection to solely rely on `window.visualViewport.scale`, which correctly reflects both browser and pinch zoom, ensuring that `chars/line` decreases when zoomed in and increases when zoomed out.

## Changes Made

### Core Functionality
- **Enhanced `fetch_data()` function** to accept stock symbol parameter instead of hardcoded "ASTS"
- **Updated shares outstanding logic** with appropriate values for each stock:
  - ASTS: 150M shares
  - ASTX: 100M shares 
  - XXRP: 80M shares

### Robustness Improvements
- **Added fallback mechanism** using realistic mock data when network requests fail
- **Enhanced error handling** to ensure the dashboard always displays useful information
- **Maintained all existing technical indicators** (RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, SMA, EMA, VWAP, ATR) for each stock

### Dashboard Features
- **Multi-stock layout**: Clean separation between stocks with professional dark theme
- **Comprehensive data**: Each stock shows OHLCV data, technical indicators, and performance metrics
- **Weekly chart views**: Separate weekly analysis for each stock
- **Percentage change calculations**: Individual performance tracking over the data period

## Before vs After

**Before:** Single stock (ASTS) dashboard with hardcoded symbol
**After:** Dynamic multi-stock dashboard supporting ASTS, ASTX, and XXRP

The dashboard now successfully displays all three requested stocks with complete technical analysis and data visualization on a single HTML page, maintaining the same professional appearance and functionality for each stock.

- Candlestick charts with technical overlays
- Volume analysis panels

**Related issues**

To align experimentation across teams and deployments, we've wrapped your SDK in a library that we distribute across the org.  This library abstracts away and standardizes most attributes that anyone would want to run an experiment against, and in doing so adds many attributes by default to each `ldcontext.Context` for evaluations. 

When profiling a few deployments for unrelated reasons, we noted that allocations in `*ValueMapBuilder.Set(...)` were usually at least visible in profiling although not egregiously so. Because we know the number of attributes we can define a capacity to pre-allocate and this would be a moderate reduction in allocations across a majority of our deployments. 

**Describe the solution you've provided**

Add a new constructor `ldcontext.NewBuilderWithCapacity(key string, capacity int)` that utilizes `ldvalue.ValueMapBuilderWithCapacity(capacity int)`. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

I got cute with functional options for a second but I reeled it in.

author: jaminh
body:
Use the values from the Via header for determining the host and port to send responses to. If the Via header can not be used fall back to the Contact header. If both the Via header and Contact header can not be used fall back to the peer host and port from the transport the message was received on.

The Contact header value is also being added to the CallInfo object. This should allow Home Assistant to save the associated URI to use for making outgoing calls, per https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3261#section-8.1.1.8.

author: youngchingjui
body:
### Problem
On mobile devices the main issues list pages (`/issues` and repository-specific `/[username]/[repo]/issues`) had fairly wide horizontal padding (coming from Tailwind's `container` padding plus our own `p-4`). This left unnecessary empty space and made content feel cramped.

### Solution
Apply smaller horizontal padding on small screens while retaining the previous spacing on larger breakpoints:

* `app/[username]/[repo]/issues/page.tsx` – change `p-4` to `p-2 sm:p-4`.
* `app/issues/page.tsx` – add `px-2 sm:px-4` to the main container and the fallback "no repos" container.

`sm` and above remains unchanged (`p-4`), so desktop/tablet layouts are identical, but mobile now gets a more generous content width.

### Notes
No functional/logic changes – just CSS class tweaks. No tests affected.

Closes #889

Removing the API documentation container from the OpenChallenges stack improves the developer experience by enabling faster deployments (local and remote), reduces energy and resource consumption, and lowers operational costs by approximately $100 per environment, per product, per year.

author: danieleschmidt
body:
## Summary
- Introduces a comprehensive configuration management system supporting YAML/JSON files and environment variables
- Replaces silent exception handling with detailed logging and specific exception management
- Improves maintainability, customization, and production reliability

## Changes

### Configuration Management
- Added `Config` class to load and merge default, user, and environment configurations
- Supports config files at `~/.docker-optimizer.yml|yaml|json` and environment variable overrides
- Configurable base image sizes, package sizes, cache settings, and layer estimation parameters
- Provides type-safe accessors and fallback values for unknown images/packages
- Added extensive tests covering config loading, merging, environment overrides, and error cases

### Error Handling & Logging
- Replaced bare `pass` statements in `external_security.py` and `performance.py` with proper exception handling
- Added contextual logging for subprocess timeouts, file not found, and generic exceptions in Trivy scanner
- Logged warnings for Dockerfile chunk processing failures
- Improved test coverage and added tests to verify error logging behavior

### Integration
- Updated `SizeEstimator` and `OptimizationCache` to use configuration values instead of hardcoded constants
- Enhanced test coverage for size estimation and external security modules

## Test plan
- [x] Unit tests for configuration loading, merging, and environment overrides
- [x] Tests for error handling and logging in external security scanner
- [x] Size estimator tests verifying config integration
- [x] Verified no silent failures; all exceptions logged with context
- [x] Maintained perfect code quality with ruff, black, and mypy
- [x] Confirmed no high/critical vulnerabilities detected

This PR significantly improves the Docker Optimizer Agent's robustness, configurability, and maintainability by addressing critical technical debt in error handling and configuration management.

🌿 Generated by [Terry](https://www.terragonlabs.com)

ℹ️ Tag @terragon-labs to ask questions and address PR feedback

Introduce a robust configuration management system with YAML/JSON file and environment variable support, enhance error handling by replacing silent failures with contextual logging and specific exception handling, integrate configuration into size estimation and caching components, and expand test coverage for these changes.

New Features:
- Add Config class for loading and merging settings from default values, YAML/JSON files, and environment variables
- Support environment variable overrides for cache, fallback sizes, and layer estimation parameters

Bug Fixes:
- Replace silent exception handlers (bare pass) in external_security.py and performance.py with specific exception handling and contextual logging

Enhancements:

body:
# Pull Request: Demo ORM với JPA + Hibernate

## Mô tả tổng quan

PR này triển khai demo ORM (Object-Relational Mapping) sử dụng JPA + Hibernate với 2 thực thể: `ClassRoom` và `Student`. Bao gồm:

- Cấu hình persistence
- Mapping entity-relationship
- DAO thao tác với DB qua `EntityManager`
- Hàm test chính (main method) kiểm tra các thao tác CRUD

---

## 1. Cấu hình `persistence.xml`

- Thiết lập kết nối database
- Khai báo persistence unit
- Kích hoạt `hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto=update` để tự tạo bảng
- Sử dụng `mysql` driver

## 2. Các Entity

- ClassRoom.java
- Student.java
- Validate trường name và age bằng annotation
- Một sinh viên thuộc 1 lớp học (ManyToOne)

## 3. DAO: StudentDAO.java

- createStudent: Thêm mới một sinh viên
- findById: Tìm sinh viên theo ID
- findAll: Lấy danh sách tất cả sinh viên
- updateStudent: Cập nhật thông tin sinh viên
- deleteStudent: Xoá sinh viên theo ID

## 4. Hàm kiểm thử (Test Main)

## Kết luận

- PR này hoàn chỉnh phần ORM cơ bản:
- Mapping OneToMany / ManyToOne
- CRUD với EntityManager
- Áp dụng validation đơn giản

The code is vulnerable to reflected XSS and XSS through exception due to user-provided values being directly included in responses without proper sanitization or escaping. Additionally, stack trace information is exposed to the user, which can reveal sensitive information about the server environment.
#### 🔸 Recommended Fix
Sanitize and escape user-provided inputs before including them in responses. Avoid exposing stack traces to the user by providing generic error messages instead.
#### 🔸 Additional Notes
The changes primarily involve encoding user-provided inputs using `encodeURIComponent` before including them in responses or log messages. This prevents potential XSS attacks by ensuring that special characters are properly escaped. Additionally, error messages have been made more generic to avoid exposing stack traces and sensitive information.

author: open-swe[bot]
body:
Fixes #485

## Overview
This PR adds a new feature to prompt users to add API keys when they are not in the allowed users list and have not configured their API keys.

### Changes
- Moved ALLOWED_USERS and isAllowedUser to @open-swe/shared package
- Created useUser hook to fetch user authentication information
- Implemented ApiKeyBanner component to display API key configuration prompt
- Integrated ApiKeyBanner into DefaultView component
- Updated import statements across the project

### Key Features
- Dismissible banner for users needing to add API keys
- Links directly to API keys settings tab
- Only shows for authenticated users not in allowed list
- Persists dismissal state using localStorage

### Rationale
This change improves user experience by providing clear guidance on API key configuration requirements, especially for users who are not pre-approved.

### Testing
- Verified build process
- Confirmed import statements work correctly
- Tested banner display logic
- Ran lint and format checks

Resolves the requirement to add a callout for users needing to configure API keys.

author: toanalien
body:
- Fix timestamps showing as `1970-01-01T00:00:00Z` in `nlm list` output
- Parse timestamps from correct positions in API response metadata
- Look for [seconds, nanos] arrays at indices 5 and 8 in metadata
- Prioritize last updated time (index 5) over creation time (index 8)
- Remove debug output and clean up parsing logic

The NotebookLM API returns timestamps as [seconds, nanoseconds] arrays
in specific metadata positions, not as single millisecond values as
previously assumed.

Fixes the issue where all notebooks showed Unix epoch timestamp,
now displays actual last modified dates for better project management.

author: vursen
body:
## Description

Moving the `initConnector` call from `ArrayUpdater#initialize` to `Grid#onAttach` removes the need for an extra call to `updateSelectionModeOnClient`. The `ArrayUpdater#initialize` method is intended for logic that needs to be skipped when detach and reattach occur within the same roundtrip. However, calling `initConnector` in that case is safe because it has a check to prevent double initialization.

## Type of change

- [x] Internal

author: superkaiba
body:
## Summary
- Implemented unified text processing pipeline that performs alignment before chunking
- Updated both PairedActivationBuffer and OrderedTextActivationBuffer to use new pipeline
- Full texts are now processed without truncation, then chunked after alignment

## Changes
1. **Created `text_processing_pipeline.py`** with:
   - `process_text_through_models()`: Processes single text through paired models
   - `process_batch_through_models()`: Processes batch of texts
   - Combines all processing steps: tokenization → activation collection → masking/normalization/alignment → chunking

2. **Updated PairedActivationBuffer**:
   - Modified `refresh()` to use new pipeline
   - Gets raw texts instead of pre-tokenized inputs
   - Processes all chunks from all texts in batch

3. **Updated OrderedTextActivationBuffer**:
   - Modified `__next__()` to use new pipeline
   - Concatenates chunks to maintain full sequences
   - Handles variable-dimension models

4. **Fixed tokenization** for single chat conversations

## Benefits
- No truncation during tokenization - full texts processed
- Proper alignment before chunking ensures token correspondence
- Modular, reusable design
- Backward compatible with existing interfaces

## Testing

### 1. Basic Functionality Tests
Created comprehensive test scripts verifying:
- Correct chunk generation
- Total tokens preserved across chunks
- Buffer functionality with new system
- 0% skip rate with same tokenizer

### 2. Llama-Qwen Alignment Testing
Added specific test for Llama-3.1-8B vs Qwen2.5-7B alignment:
- **100% success rate** on all test cases
- Semantic alignment correctly handles tokenizer differences
- Chunking after alignment preserves all tokens
- Confirms the implementation works for the critical cross-model case

### 3. Real Data Testing
Tested with actual pile and lmsys data:
- **71 sequences processed** with 0% skip rate
- **Long text chunking verified**: 3,174 characters → 5 chunks of ~128 tokens each
- **Real data compatibility confirmed**: Successfully loaded and processed `pile_lmsys_config`
- Works with both chat format and plain text data

Test output summary:
```
RESULTS:
  Batches processed: 5
  Total chunks generated: 10
  Sequences processed: 71
  Sequences skipped: 0
  Skip rate: 0.00%

✅ Core chunking functionality VERIFIED\!
The implementation correctly:
  - Processes texts without truncation
  - Chunks after processing (not before)
  - Maintains all tokens across chunks
  - Works with the activation buffer system
```

Fixes #597

author: bulkbeing
body:
Tokio runtime automatically spins up N number of worker threads based on the available cpu cores. In a k8s environment, this value is calculated based on the `resources.limits.cpu` value. If it is not set, the worker thread count will be equivalent to the logical cores available on the host node. On a node with 32 cores, the memory usage of numa container stays at around 120MB to 140MB when `resources.limits.cpu` is not set. If set explicitly to 1 CPU or less, the memory usage stays around 20MB.

The `NUMAFLOW_CPU_REQUEST` environment variable is set by the controller as a reference to the `resource.requests.cpu`. We can not use the `NUMAFLOW_CPU_LIMITS` (references `resources.limits.cpu`) value, since its value will be host's logical core count if not set explicitly. User may specify a higher value by setting NUMAFLOW_CPU_REQUEST in `containerTemplate.env` section for the vertex.

This PR also rearranges build args (like `GIT_COMMIT_ID`) in `Dockerfile` to avoid build cache invalidation.

author: koichi98
body:
## Description
Add poll method

## Related links
nvme_poll
https://github.com/openbsd/src/blob/f27f14072d0d9ed1a84afd679d3fef0ac483f421/sys/dev/ic/nvme.c#L1128

nvme_poll_fill
https://github.com/openbsd/src/blob/f27f14072d0d9ed1a84afd679d3fef0ac483f421/sys/dev/ic/nvme.c#L1164

nvme_poll_done
https://github.com/openbsd/src/blob/f27f14072d0d9ed1a84afd679d3fef0ac483f421/sys/dev/ic/nvme.c#L1173

## How was this PR tested?

## Notes for reviewers

#### CCB Structure in Device Drivers
In device drivers, the CCB (Command Control Block) structure is used to manage I/O commands received from the kernel and device information queries (identify commands) on a one-to-one basis. These CCBs are exclusively managed within the device driver. During initialization, CCBs are allocated as an array (ccbs_alloc), and at runtime, the ccb_list (free list) stores the indices of currently available CCBs within the ccbs array.

#### Design Choice for nvme_poll in Awkernel
While OpenBSD's nvme_poll function takes a pointer to CCB as an argument, Awkernel's implementation simply takes a ccb_id (index). This design choice is based on the nature of the ccbs array:

- It is a fixed-size array, meaning its length does not change.
- The order of its elements is stable; they do not get reordered.

Therefore, knowing just the index is sufficient for a process to identify the CCB.

This approach also addresses a Rust constraint: it's not possible to simultaneously pass both a mutable reference to the entire ccbs array (&mut ccbs) and a mutable reference to one of its elements (&mut ccb) as arguments to a function.

body:
This PR implements a sophisticated multi-agent architecture to improve game master responses and prevent common tabletop RPG mistakes through a structured three-agent pipeline.

## Overview

The implementation replaces the single GameMaster agent with a coordinated pipeline:

**Player Input** → **Planning Agent** → **Game Master Agent** → **Editor Agent** → **Final Response**

## Key Features

### 🤖 Three Specialized Agents

- **Planning Agent**: Analyzes player input, validates actions within game rules, and creates structured plans while ensuring player agency is respected
- **Game Master Agent**: Converts structured plans into engaging narrative responses with proper tabletop RPG tone and atmosphere  
- **Editor Agent**: Reviews and improves responses to prevent common mistakes like rolling dice for players or taking unauthorized actions

### 🔧 Configuration Flexibility

```json
{
  "UseMultiAgentMode": true,  // Enable multi-agent pipeline (default)
  "Ollama": { /* ... */ }
}
```

Users can switch between multi-agent and single-agent modes for backward compatibility.

### 📝 Clean Chat History Management

Only the final edited response is stored in chat history. Intermediate planning and draft responses are:
- Logged for observability and debugging
- Used internally for agent coordination  
- **Not persisted** to avoid cluttering conversation history

### 🛡️ Player Agency Protection

Multiple checkpoints throughout the pipeline ensure:
- Agents never roll dice for the player
- No actions taken on behalf of the player without permission
- Player decision-making is always respected
- Game rules violations are caught early

### 📊 Comprehensive Observability

```
[System] Generating response...
[System] Planning response...
[System] Creating narrative response...
[System] Editing and improving response...
GameMaster: [Final polished response]
```

Full logging at each pipeline stage with visual feedback in the console.

## Technical Implementation

### Agent Coordination

```csharp
public async Task<ChatHistory> ChatAsync(ChatHistory history, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
{
    // Step 1: Planning Agent creates structured plan
    string plan = await GetPlanningResponse(history, cancellationToken);
    
    // Step 2: Game Master Agent creates narrative response  
    string gmResponse = await GetGameMasterResponse(history, plan, cancellationToken);
    
    // Step 3: Editor Agent improves the response
    string finalResponse = await GetEditorResponse(gmResponse, cancellationToken);
    
    // Only final response goes to chat history
    history.Add(new ChatMessageContent(AuthorRole.Assistant, finalResponse));
    return history;
}
```

### Backward Compatibility

- Maintains existing `IConsoleChatClient` interface
- Single-agent mode available via configuration
- All existing functionality preserved

## Testing

Added comprehensive test coverage:
- 18 total tests (all passing)
- Individual agent creation and configuration
- Multi-agent pipeline coordination
- Prevention of common tabletop RPG mistakes
- Configuration switching between modes

## Benefits

1. **Prevents Common Mistakes**: Multi-layer review catches dice rolling violations and player agency issues
2. **Improved Response Quality**: Specialized agents focus on their expertise areas
3. **Better Observability**: Comprehensive logging and visual feedback at each stage
4. **Maintainable Architecture**: Clear separation of concerns, individually testable agents
5. **Flexible Configuration**: Easy switching between single and multi-agent modes

## Documentation

- Created detailed `MULTI_AGENT_ARCHITECTURE.md` with implementation specifics
- Updated existing documentation to reflect new capabilities
- Comprehensive inline code documentation

This PR introduces Redux Toolkit to replace React Context for state management in the Moringa Lost & Found application.

### 📋 Changes Made

#### **Dependencies Added**
-  - Modern Redux with built-in best practices
-  - React bindings for Redux

#### **New Files Created**
-  - Main Redux store configuration
-  - Items state management with async thunks
-  - UI state management (modal, loading, errors)

#### **Updated Components**
- **main.jsx**: Added Redux Provider, removed ItemProvider
- **App.jsx**: Updated to use Redux for modal state management
- **ItemsGrid.jsx**: Updated to use Redux for items data and loading states
- **ReportModal.jsx**: Updated to use Redux for adding items and modal state

#### **Key Features**
- ✅ **Async Thunks**: , , , 
- ✅ **Redux Hooks**: , 
- ✅ **State Management**: Items, loading states, errors, modal visibility
- ✅ **Error Handling**: Comprehensive error states and retry functionality
- ✅ **Type Safety**: Proper state structure and action types

### 🔄 Migration Details
- **Removed**: React Context (ItemProvider) and useItems hook
- **Added**: Redux store with slices for items and UI state
- **Updated**: All components now use Redux hooks instead of Context
- **Maintained**: All existing functionality and user experience

### 🧪 Testing
- All existing functionality preserved
- Error handling improved with retry capabilities
- Loading states properly managed
- Modal functionality maintained

### 📊 Benefits
- **Scalability**: Better state management for growing application
- **Maintainability**: Centralized state with predictable updates
- **Performance**: Optimized re-rendering with Redux
- **Developer Experience**: Better debugging with Redux DevTools support

### 🎯 Ready for Review
This PR is ready for review and testing. All existing functionality has been preserved while upgrading to Redux Toolkit.

#180 180
This pull request includes updates to fix bugs, improve firewall configuration logic, and adjust network settings in the XRAYUI project. Key changes include bug fixes mentioned in the changelog, enhanced handling of firewall rules, and a minor adjustment to network type settings.

### Bug Fixes (Changelog Updates):
* Added a new version entry `0.54.1` to `CHANGELOG.md`, documenting fixes for XRAY not working in `REDIRECT` mode and the inability to save the `HTTPUpgrade` network type in the Transport window.

### Firewall Configuration Enhancements:
* Updated `configure_firewall()` in `firewall.sh` to check for and load the `xt_socket` module before adding the transparent `DIVERT` hook. Logs a warning if the module is missing.
* Modified `configure_firewall_client()` in `firewall.sh` to use a broader match for firewall rules (`TPROXY`, `DNAT`, or `REDIRECT`) and removed redundant conditional nesting for cleaner logic.

### Network Type Settings Adjustment:
* Updated `NET_KEEP` in `CommonObjects.ts` to remove `httpupgradeSettings` from the `http` network type and assign it exclusively to the `httpupgrade` type, ensuring proper categorization.

Closes #72
/claim #72
## Purpose

Implement a comprehensive data replication plugin for StarbaseDB that enables users to pull data from external databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, etc.) into the internal SQLite database with configurable sync intervals and incremental updates.

This addresses the request for creating a "pull mechanism" to replicate data from external sources like Supabase PostgreSQL into StarbaseDB's edge-close SQLite replica.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b44e78c6-0e76-4cde-a489-e4ab87e23a96


## Tasks

<!-- [x] complete; [ ] incomplete -->

- [x] Create DataReplicationPlugin following StarbaseDB plugin architecture
- [x] Implement external database connection support (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Hyperdrive)
- [x] Add incremental sync mechanism using tracking columns (id, created_at, updated_at)
- [x] Create configurable sync intervals per replication configuration
- [x] Build comprehensive REST API for replication management
- [x] Add real-time logging and monitoring system
- [x] Implement event callback system for external integrations
- [x] Create internal database tables for configuration and logs storage
- [x] Add proper error handling and graceful degradation
- [x] Write unit tests and comprehensive documentation
- [x] Register plugin in main application with event handling
- [x] Deploy and test on live Cloudflare Workers environment

## Verify

<!-- guidance or steps to assist the reviewer -->

### 🔍 Code Review Checklist
- **Plugin Architecture**: Verify adherence to StarbaseDB plugin patterns in `plugins/data-replication/index.ts`
- **External Database Security**: Review credential handling and SQL injection prevention
- **API Endpoints**: Test all 7 REST endpoints with proper authentication
- **TypeScript Types**: Validate type safety and interface compliance
- **Error Handling**: Ensure graceful degradation and comprehensive logging

### 🧪 Testing Steps
1. **Build & Deploy**: `npm run build && npx wrangler deploy`
2. **Configure Replication**:
   ```bash
   curl -X POST https://starbasedb.mavrickrishi.workers.dev/data-replication/configure \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer ABC123" \
     -d '{"name":"test","sourceConfig":{"dialect":"postgresql","host":"demo.supabase.co","port":5432,"user":"postgres","password":"demo-pass","database":"postgres"},"targetTable":"users","sourceTable":"users","syncIntervalMinutes":30,"trackingColumn":"updated_at"}'
   ```
3. **Check Status**: `curl -X GET https://starbasedb.mavrickrishi.workers.dev/data-replication/status -H "Authorization: Bearer ABC123"`
4. **Monitor Logs**: View Cloudflare Workers dashboard for real-time sync events

### 📊 Performance Verification
- **Memory**: Plugin reuses existing connection infrastructure (minimal overhead)
- **Scalability**: Supports multiple concurrent replication configurations
- **Efficiency**: Incremental sync with WHERE clause filtering

## Before

**GitHub Issue #72 Request:**
- No data replication functionality
- No external database sync capability  
- Manual data management required
- No edge-close replica creation

**StarbaseDB Plugin Ecosystem:**
```
plugins/
├── cdc/           # Change Data Capture
├── cron/          # Scheduled tasks  
├── query-log/     # Query logging
├── stats/         # System statistics
└── [missing data replication]
```

## After

**✅ Complete Data Replication System:**

### 🔌 **New Plugin Added**
```
plugins/data-replication/
├── index.ts       # Main plugin (475+ lines)
├── index.test.ts  # Unit tests (3 passing)
├── meta.json      # Plugin metadata
└── README.md      # Comprehensive docs
```

### 🚀 **Live Deployment**
- **URL**: https://starbasedb.mavrickrishi.workers.dev
- **Status**: ✅ Successfully deployed and tested
- **Plugin**: ✅ Registered and running

### 📡 **7 New API Endpoints**
- `POST /data-replication/configure` - Set up replication
- `POST /data-replication/start/:name` - Start specific replication  
- `POST /data-replication/stop/:name` - Stop specific replication
- `POST /data-replication/sync/:name` - Manual sync trigger
- `GET /data-replication/status` - View all configurations
- `GET /data-replication/logs` - Sync operation logs
- `DELETE /data-replication/configure/:name` - Remove config

### 💾 **Database Schema**
Two new internal tables created:
- `tmp_replication_configs` - Store replication settings
- `tmp_replication_logs` - Track sync operations and performance

### 🔄 **Working Demo**
```bash
# ✅ TESTED: Configuration successful
{"result":{"success":true,"message":"Replication configured successfully"}}

# ✅ TESTED: Status shows active replication
{"result":{"configs":[{"name":"supabase-users","is_running":true,"sync_interval_minutes":30}]}}
```

### 🎯 **Issue Requirements Met**
✅ Pull mechanism for external databases  
✅ Configurable sync intervals  
✅ Table-specific replication  
✅ Incremental updates via tracking columns  
✅ Supabase PostgreSQL support  
✅ Edge-close SQLite replica creation  
✅ wrangler.toml configuration support

## Purpose
<!-- Describe the intention of the changes being proposed. What problem does it solve or functionality does it add? -->

This pull request introduces support for deploying AI model configurations in the Azure Cognitive Services infrastructure. The changes primarily focus on adding a new parameter for AI model deployments and updating the deployment logic to handle these configurations and support for existing AI projects.

### Enhancements to AI model deployment:

* Added a new `aiModelDeployments` parameter of type `array` in `infra/deploy_foundry_role_assignment.bicep` to define multiple AI model configurations.
* Introduced a new resource loop in `infra/deploy_foundry_role_assignment.bicep` to create deployments for each AI model in `aiModelDeployments`, including properties such as model name, RAI policy, and SKU details.
* Updated the `assignOpenAIRoleToAISearch` module in `infra/deploy_ai_foundry.bicep` to pass the `aiModelDeployments` parameter.

### Infrastructure template updates:

* Modified `infra/main.json` to include the `aiModelDeployments` parameter, defaulting to an empty array, and updated the deployment logic to iterate over the models and create corresponding resources.

## Does this introduce a breaking change?
<!-- Mark one with an "x". -->

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

  * `feat`: A new feature
  * `fix`: A bug fix

  * `refactor`: A code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature

-->

- [x] For frontend changes, I have pulled the latest code from main, built the frontend, and committed all static files.

body:
This improvement addresses an issue in the Italian e-invoicing (l10n_it_edi) and IAP registration logic where incoming vendor bills with only a VAT number failed to match the correct registered EDI user.

Changes introduced:
- Added `edi_identification_secondary` (e.g. VAT number) to support fallback user matching.
- Updated the `/create_user` endpoint to accept and store the secondary identifier.
- Modified `create_user` logic to send both primary and secondary IDs from Odoo.
- Prepared the base for matching incoming invoices against both identifiers.

See also: odoo/iap-apps#1056

author: sanyam-singh
body:
This commit introduces a new feature that uses an OpenAI LLM to predict weather alerts for a given location and list of crops.

The new feature is implemented in `src/mcp_weather_server/tools/openai_llm.py`. It gets weather data and then makes a call to the OpenAI API to generate a weather alert.

The server has been updated to integrate the new feature, and a new test has been added to ensure it works correctly. The dependencies have also been updated.

# feat: 3단계 - Storybook 설치 및 UI 컴포넌트 시스템 구축

## 🎯 작업 목표
3단계 작업으로 Storybook을 설치하고 디자인 토큰을 활용한 공통 UI 컴포넌트 시스템을 구축했습니다.

## ✨ 주요 변경사항

### 1. Storybook 설치 및 설정
- **Storybook 9.0.18** 설치 및 초기 설정
- **Tailwind CSS 연동**: 디자인 토큰과 연동하여 일관된 스타일링 지원
- **애드온 추가**:
  - `@storybook/addon-a11y`: 접근성 검사
  - `@storybook/addon-vitest`: 컴포넌트 테스트 지원
- **설정 파일**:
  - `.storybook/main.ts`: Storybook 메인 설정
  - `.storybook/preview.ts`: Tailwind CSS 및 디자인 토큰 import
  - `.storybook/vitest.setup.ts`: Vitest 테스트 설정

### 2. 공통 UI 컴포넌트 생성

#### Button 컴포넌트
- **5가지 variant**: `primary`, `secondary`, `outline`, `ghost`, `danger`
- **3가지 size**: `sm`, `md`, `lg`
- **상태 지원**: `disabled`, `fullWidth`
- **접근성**: focus ring, keyboard navigation 지원

#### Input 컴포넌트
- **다양한 타입**: `text`, `email`, `password`, `number`, `tel`, `url`
- **상태 관리**: `error`, `disabled`, `required`
- **레이블 및 도움말**: `label`, `helperText` 지원
- **크기 옵션**: `sm`, `md`, `lg`

#### Card 컴포넌트
- **3가지 variant**: `default`, `elevated`, `outlined`
- **4가지 패딩**: `none`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`
- **하위 컴포넌트**: `CardHeader`, `CardTitle`, `CardSubtitle`, `CardContent`, `CardFooter`
- **인터랙티브 모드**: hover, active 상태 지원

### 3. 디자인 토큰 활용
- **일관된 스타일링**: 모든 컴포넌트에서 디자인 토큰의 색상, 간격, 타이포그래피 활용
- **프로젝트 규칙 준수**: Tailwind 클래스만 사용하는 스타일링 방식 통일
- **CSS 변수 연동**: `--color-primary-*`, `--spacing-*`, `--font-*` 등 활용

### 4. Storybook 스토리 작성
- **각 컴포넌트별 다양한 스토리**: variant, size, 상태별 예시
- **Controls 지원**: 실시간 속성 변경 가능
- **AutoDocs**: 자동 문서화
- **레이아웃 최적화**: centered layout으로 컴포넌트 시각화

## 📁 생성된 파일 구조
src/components/ui/
├── Button.tsx + Button.stories.tsx
├── Input.tsx + Input.stories.tsx
├── Card.tsx + Card.stories.tsx
└── index.ts (export 관리)
.storybook/
├── main.ts (설정)
├── preview.ts (Tailwind CSS 연동)
└── vitest.setup.ts (테스트 설정)


## 🚀 사용 방법
1. **Storybook 실행**: `npm run storybook`
2. **컴포넌트 사용**:
   ```tsx
   import { Button, Input, Card } from '@/components/ui';
   
   // Button 사용 예시
   <Button variant="primary" size="md">Click me</Button>
   
   // Input 사용 예시
   <Input label="Email" type="email" placeholder="Enter email" />
   
   // Card 사용 예시
   <Card variant="elevated">
     <CardHeader>
       <CardTitle>Title</CardTitle>
     </CardHeader>
     <CardContent>Content</CardContent>
   </Card>
   ```

## �� 테스트 및 검증
- **Storybook**: `http://localhost:6006/`에서 모든 컴포넌트 확인 가능
- **접근성**: a11y 애드온을 통한 접근성 검사
- **테스트**: Vitest 애드온을 통한 컴포넌트 테스트 지원

## 📋 체크리스트
- [x] Storybook 설치 및 설정 완료
- [x] Tailwind CSS 연동 완료
- [x] 공통 UI 컴포넌트 생성 완료
- [x] 디자인 토큰 활용 완료
- [x] Storybook 스토리 작성 완료
- [x] 프로젝트 규칙 준수 (Tailwind 클래스만 사용)
- [x] 접근성 고려
- [x] 테스트 환경 구축

## 🔗 관련 이슈
#10 Storybook 설치 및 UI 컴포넌트 시스템 구축

---

이 PR은 디자인 시스템의 기반을 마련하고, 개발자들이 일관된 UI 컴포넌트를 쉽게 사용할 수 있도록 도와줍니다.

author: aethr
body:
## Description

Previously, the omAgLulucfWasteEmis.py module was using an intermediate reprojected version of the Australian land use file, which was generated using the wrong projection.

This PR adapts the `remap_raster` utility to allow an alternative input CRS to be specified, so that we can use the utility to regrid the land use raster onto the domain grid. The result then has the land mask applied so that all sectoral emissions are applied within valid land pixels.

Based on commits originally authored by @prayner in #42.

## About the PR
This PR fixes the door remaining waterlogged after closing it or activating the shields.

## Why / Balance
Because there should be no water continuing to flow inside the TARDIS after the doors have been closed or the shields activated.

I'm not 100% confident about the locations where I disable the waterlogged property.

## Summary

This PR fixes E2E test failures by refactoring the `structured_output_schema` parameter from `Optional[Dict[str, Any]]` to `Optional[str]` across all tool definitions. The root cause was that MCP (Model Context Protocol) can only transmit strings between client and server, not Python objects.

## Changes

### Core Fix
- Changed `structured_output_schema` parameter type from Dict to str in all tool definitions
- Added JSON parsing in executor.py to convert string schemas back to dicts for adapter use
- This resolves FastMCP validation errors where schemas were being received as None

### Gemini API Fixes
- Fixed Gemini function response role from "model" to "user" per API requirements
- Added documentation about Gemini's limited JSON Schema support (no pattern constraints)
- Added JSON extraction utility to handle responses wrapped in markdown

### Test Infrastructure
- Fixed all unit and integration tests to match new string parameter type
- Added comprehensive tests for JSON extraction utility
- Fixed test isolation issues by adding victoria-logs-data/ to .gitignore

### Additional Improvements
- Added PARSING error category to Grok adapter
- Improved error handling for Vertex AI initialization
- Updated E2E test scenarios for better reliability

## Test Results

All test suites passing:
- ✅ Unit tests: 390 passed
- ✅ Integration tests: All passed  
- ✅ MCP integration tests: 18 passed
- ✅ E2E tests: Fixed and passing
- ✅ Pre-push hooks: All passing

## Impact

This change is backwards compatible at the MCP protocol level since LLMs always send strings via MCP. The refactoring properly handles the protocol requirements while maintaining the same functionality.

body:
This PR implements comprehensive improvements to prevent formatting and quality issues from reaching PR review, addressing the root cause of review churn described in the issue.

## Problem

AI contributors were frequently submitting PRs with formatting and linting issues that should have been caught by running the same checks that CI runs locally. This created unnecessary review cycles focused on mechanical fixes rather than substantive code review.

## Solution

Added multiple layers of quality check enforcement:

### 1. Enhanced AI Instructions (`.github/copilot-instructions.md`)
- **Step 6**: Now explicitly requires running `poetry run ruff format .` and `poetry run ruff check .` after every change
- **PR Completeness Checklist**: Added mandatory checks for local formatting and linting validation
- **New Local Development Section**: Comprehensive workflow guidance with specific commands

### 2. Local CI Check Script (`scripts/local-ci-check.sh`)
```bash
# Replicates exact CI pipeline checks locally
./scripts/local-ci-check.sh apps/your-app
./scripts/local-ci-check.sh libs/your-lib
```
- Runs dependency installation, formatting, linting, and testing
- Provides clear success/failure feedback with actionable error messages
- Tested successfully on both apps and libraries

### 3. Improved Issue Templates
- **Feature Request Template**: Added required checkbox for local CI validation
- **Implementation Details**: Enhanced with examples emphasizing quality check requirements
- Ensures AI contributors validate locally before submission

### 4. Pre-commit Hooks (`.pre-commit-config.yaml`)
- Optional automation for teams wanting automatic quality validation
- Runs ruff formatting/linting, file quality checks, and ADR status validation
- Targets Python projects in apps/ and libs/ directories

### 5. Documentation Updates
- **Main README**: Added quality assurance section with clear commands
- **Scripts README**: Documented local CI check script usage and purpose

## Validation

- ✅ Script tested successfully on `libs/hoopstat-config` and `apps/example-calculator-app`
- ✅ Proper error handling with helpful usage messages
- ✅ Pre-commit configuration validates syntactically
- ✅ No breaking changes to existing functionality

## Expected Impact

These changes create a comprehensive quality gate system that should significantly reduce PR review cycles focused on mechanical formatting/linting issues, allowing reviewers to focus on substantive code improvements.

author: ferenc-
body:
The `hostapd-WiFi7.conf` at line 12 rightfully instructs users
    to compile hostapd and the `Upgrade_hostapd.md` to get the sources
    from git://w1.fi/srv/git/hostap.git.
    After inspecting these sources, it becomes evident that
    `ht_coex` is a non-exisitent option in the upstream repo
    and trying to start a compiled `hostapd` with this config option,
    will fail for the very same reason.
    Further investigation suggests, that the patch that does make,
    `ht_coex` available has been made by Felix Fietkau
    and it is only included in a few downstream packages like OpenWrt.
    Furthermore inspecting the patch reveals that `ht_coex=0` setting is
    logically equivalent of not having the patch at all,
    hence the suggestion here is to simply remove this option from the config file.
    Instead of patching the upstream repo for no real benefit.

author: florianl
body:
Add support to dynamically attach to symbols of executables.

E.g. to inspect memory allocations in Go one could attach a uprobe to runtime.mallocgc:

```
sudo ./ebpf-profiler -collection-agent=127.0.0.1:11000 -disable-tls -off-cpu-threshold 0.1 -uprobe /path/to/my/go/executable:runtime.mallocgc
```

Another interesting uprobe in Go executables is runtime.gopark, that puts a Go routine into a waiting state.

To identify potential uprobes, one could use something like this:
```
bpftrace -l 'uprobe:/path/to/my/executable:*'
```

Visualize uprobes with https://github.com/elastic/devfiler

author: funamayukina
body: ## Issue - resolve: ## Why is this change needed? The Drizzle PostgreSQL parser was missing support for table-level CHECK and UNIQUE constraints, while MySQL parser already supported them. This created inconsistency between database parsers and limited PostgreSQL schema parsing capabilities. ### 1. CHECK Constraints Support Added support for parsing CHECK constraints in PostgreSQL tables using the `check('constraint_name', sql 'condition')` syntax. This enables validation rules like age limits, string length requirements, and custom business logic constraints to be properly parsed and displayed in ERD visualizations. https://liam-app-git-feat-drizzle-postgres-table-constraints-liambx.vercel.app/erd/p/github.com/FunamaYukina/drizzle-sample-schema/blob/main/drizzle/mysql/advanced/schema.ts?showMode=ALL_FIELDS&active=users ### 2. Table-level UNIQUE Constraints Support Implemented parsing for table-level UNIQUE constraints using the `unique('constraint_name').on(table.column1, table.column2)` syntax. This allows composite unique constraints across multiple columns to be correctly identified and processed, with proper mapping from JavaScript property names to database column names. https://liam-app-git-feat-drizzle-postgres-table-constraints-liambx.vercel.app/erd/p/github.com/FunamaYukina/drizzle-sample-schema/blob/main/drizzle/mysql/advanced/schema.ts?showMode=ALL_FIELDS&active=bookings

author: ishaaq-21
body:
## Bug Fix: Some Invisible Lines in Spider Component Due to line Filter

### Summary
This pull request resolves a rendering issue in the `Spider` component where certain icon connector lines became invisible on hover.

### How I Found the Bug
While customizing the `Spider` component for my own use case, I noticed that **lines at specific angles** (0° and 90°) would disappear when hovered. This led me to investigate the SVG filter definitions applied to those lines.

### Details
- The issue occurred with lines positioned at **cardinal angles**:
  - The **vertical line** from the center to the top icon
  - The **horizontal line** connecting icons at the bottom edge
- On hover, an SVG-based **glow effect** caused these lines to become invisible
- This was due to how filters blend layers when elements are perfectly aligned with pixel boundaries

### Fix
- Removed the SVG `<filter>` that was causing the blending issue
- Eliminated its usage from the affected line components

### Rationale
Since the glow effect added **minimal visual enhancement** and introduced **critical rendering bugs**, it was removed to ensure:
- **Consistent visibility** of all lines
- **Better customization experience** for users adapting the component

 Bug identified through real use  
Cleaner rendering without visual regression  
Better UX when customizing the component

author: gradkh
body:
### TL;DR

Added direct conversion from `AESTowerField8b` to both `BinaryField128bGhash` and `BinaryField128bPolyval` using lookup tables.

### What changed?

- Implemented `From<AESTowerField8b>` for `BinaryField128bGhash` using a 256-entry lookup table
- Implemented `From<AESTowerField8b>` for `BinaryField128bPolyval` using a 256-entry lookup table
- Added tests to verify that the direct conversions are consistent with the existing indirect conversion paths
- Added tests to ensure multiplication consistency when converting between fields

### How to test?

Run the new tests that verify:
- Direct conversion from `AESTowerField8b` matches the indirect conversion through `AESTowerField128b`
- Multiplication consistency is preserved when converting between fields

```bash
cargo test --package field --lib -- ghash::tests::tests_conversion_from_aes8 polyval::tests::tests_conversion_from_aes8
```

### Why make this change?

This change optimizes field conversions by providing direct paths from `AESTowerField8b` to both `BinaryField128bGhash` and `BinaryField128bPolyval`. Using lookup tables for these 8-bit to 128-bit conversions is more efficient than going through intermediate conversions, especially since there are only 256 possible input values. This should improve performance in cryptographic operations that require these field conversions.

author: mihaipop-tsa
body:
This PR resolves an error caused by the removal of the [stylus](https://www.npmjs.com/package/stylus) `npm` package from the registry due to a security vulnerability.

`yarn install` was failing with a "404 Not Found" error for `stylus@0.59.0`. This package was identified as a transitive dependency pulled in by `@angular-devkit/build-angular`.

To mitigate this without upgrading major dependencies, this change adds a `resolutions` entry to `frontend/package.json`. This forces Yarn to resolve the stylus dependency to `0.0.1-security`, which is the official, empty placeholder package published by the `npm` security team.

The yarn.lock file has been updated to reflect this resolution.

body:
This PR contains all the fresh fixes for the issues found by vault audits as well as fresh fixes for triggerable withdrawals (e.g fix for https://research.lido.fi/t/security-disclosure-post-mortem-csverifier-weak-validation-of-the-historical-block-gindex-user-funds-remain-safe/10466)

Lido: 
- storage migrated in new slots to prevent misleading offchain tooling
- events are sorted out
- rebalancing use shares instead of ether

Accounting: 
- return `simulatedShareRate` to the report to fix WQ handling
- reorder calls on applying report to prevent invoking callbacks mid-state

LazyOracle: 
- Quarantine was fixed and rewritten for more clarity
- More sanity checks

StakingVault:
- fix ossification check
- prevent any other similar attack by limiting vaults by factory, not codehash

PDG:
- compensation is now permissionless and directly to the vault

VaultHub:
- Redemptions are now in shares and mostly redesigned
- Obligations include forced rebalances, redemptions and unpaid fees
- Bad debt socializing and internalizing improved
- Minimal reserve is introduced
- Safer disconnection
- Locked is now calculated dynamically from maxLiabilityShares and minimalReserve
- maxLiabilityShares is used for safer unlocking
- inOutDelta is cached for last two refslots now

OperatorGrid:
- added syncTier method to update vault params from tier
- added jail mechanics
- moved `updateShareLimit` and `updateFees` from VaultHub here

VaultFactory:
- having a registry of deployed vaults
- fix setting wrong nodeOperatorFee recipient

author: knowald
body:
## Summary

  This PR adds validation to reject invalid duration units (like `d`, `w`, `mo`, `y`) when used
   with the `CERTIFICATE_EXPIRATION` condition. Go's `time.Duration` only supports units up to
  hours (`h`), so using larger units like days would silently fail and evaluate to 0.

## Problem

Previously, when users attempted to use conditions like:
```yaml
conditions:
  - "[CERTIFICATE_EXPIRATION] > 14d"
 ```

The `14d` would fail to parse as a valid duration and default to 0, causing the condition to
behave unexpectedly without any clear error message.

Related issues:
- https://github.com/TwiN/gatus/issues/183
- https://github.com/TwiN/gatus/pull/50
- https://github.com/TwiN/gatus/issues/246
- https://github.com/TwiN/gatus/pull/285

## Solution

Added validation that:
1. Detects invalid duration units during condition validation
2. Returns an error message suggesting the use of hours instead

## Example Error Message

When using an invalid duration unit:
`invalid duration unit in condition '[CERTIFICATE_EXPIRATION] > 14d': Go's time.Duration only supports units up to 'h' (hours). Use hours instead (e.g., '336h' instead of '14d')`

## Changes

- Added `isDurationWithInvalidUnit()` helper to detect invalid duration formats
- Updated `Condition.Validate()` to check for invalid units in CERTIFICATE_EXPIRATION
conditions

- [x] Tested and/or added tests to validate that the changes work as intended, if applicable.
- [ ] Updated documentation in `README.md`, if applicable.

body: **Description:** This pull request addresses several critical UI/UX issues found on the registration/signup page to improve usability and visual consistency. **What was the problem?** - Logo Not Visible: The logo image in the header was not rendering correctly on the signup page, displaying only the alt text. This was due to an incorrect relative file path. - Page Not Scrollable: On screens with limited height, the form content was cut off at the bottom because the page was not configured to allow vertical scrolling. - Navbar Overlap: The fixed header was overlapping the top of the form, hiding the title and first few input fields. **What was the solution?** - Fixed Logo Path: The src attribute for the logo image was updated to a root-relative path (/assets/images/vehigologo.png) to ensure it consistently loads on all pages. - Enabled Scrolling: The overflow-y: auto; property was added to the html and body selectors in style.css, allowing the page to correctly display a scrollbar when content exceeds the viewport height. - Resolved Navbar Overlap: A padding-top of 100px was added to the body element in style.css. This pushes all page content down, creating enough space to prevent it from being hidden behind the fixed header. **Screenshot:** Closes #14

body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting pull request to Airlift -->

* Extract a method to get a single secret value
  * This is a narrower version of (private) `resolveConfiguration` and the (public) `getResolvedConfiguration`; the latter two take a value or a whole `Map` of values with potentially many secrets references, parse them and invoke a relevant secrets provider for each encountered reference. The new method explicitly takes the provider name and a single key, which is much more focused and also sometimes useful.
* Provide a way to use a different source of secrets resolvers
  * We don't always have the ability to package the secrets resolvers into a neat `Map` - sometimes we'd like to decide what to do only once we encounter a specific provider name.

<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

This PR adds support for supply frequency sensors in Tuya energy monitoring devices (dlq and zndb categories). Supply frequency is an important electrical parameter that indicates the AC frequency of the power supply, typically 50Hz or 60Hz depending on the region.

The changes include:
1. Added `SUPPLY_FREQUENCY` to the DPCode enum in `const.py`
2. Added frequency sensor definitions for both dlq and zndb device categories
3. Added translation key "supply_frequency" with the name "Supply frequency"
4. Updated test fixtures to include supply frequency data
5. Updated snapshots to reflect the new sensor entities

This enhancement allows users to monitor the supply frequency of their electrical systems, which can be useful for:
- Power quality monitoring
- Electrical system diagnostics
- Regional power grid analysis
- Detection of frequency variations that may indicate grid issues

author: kristjanvalur
body:
Normally asyncio ignored CancelledError exceptions in Tasks.  asyncSlots create tasks, but the way that the error handler is implemented, by invoking the Future.result(), this CancelledError is re-raised and then logged by the QT core.
This PR silences CancelledErrors, such as can occur on the end of application or when cancelling long running operations.

This pull request introduces significant updates to the Mosaico Python video generation framework, focusing on improving image handling, adding comprehensive tests, and providing detailed documentation. Key changes include the addition of a new `CLAUDE.md` file for developer guidance, enhancements to the `ImageAsset` clip-making process to support transparency, and extensive unit tests for image-related functionality.

### Documentation Updates:

* Added `CLAUDE.md` file with detailed developer guidance, including commands for package management, code quality checks, testing, and documentation building. It also provides an architecture overview, key patterns, and AI integration details for the Mosaico framework.

### Image Handling Enhancements:

* Updated `_make_clip` method in `src/mosaico/clip_makers/image.py` to handle PNG transparency by switching image decoding from `cv.IMREAD_COLOR` to `cv.IMREAD_UNCHANGED`. Also changed temporary file suffix from `.jpg` to `.png`.

### Testing Improvements:

* Added comprehensive unit tests in `tests/clip_makers/test_image.py` to cover various scenarios for `ImageClipMaker`, including handling transparent and opaque PNGs, resizing behavior, relative positioning, and background asset handling. Tests also validate the `_resize_and_crop` utility for resizing and cropping images while preserving channels and handling different image formats.

body:
[…project: true](fix: normalize tsconfigRootDir to handle trailing path separators in project: true)

Fixes #11413

When using project: true, the search for tsconfig.json files would stop prematurely if 	sconfigRootDir contained a trailing path separator. This was due to an incorrect length comparison that included the trailing separator character.

The fix normalizes the tsconfigRootDir path and removes trailing separators before comparing lengths, ensuring consistent behavior regardless of whether the path ends with '/' or '\'.

Changes:
- Modified getProjectConfigFiles to normalize tsconfigRootDir path
- Added test case to verify fix works with trailing separators
- Maintains backward compatibility with existing functionality
